headline: 7 killed, 20 injured in gas cylinder blast at Ashulia factory
summary: A massive explosion in a covered van carrying gas cylinders triggered a fire that destroyed several vehicles and caused widespread destruction in Savar.
details: At least seven people were killed and 20 others injured after a gas cylinder-carrying covered van exploded and caught fire at a garment factory premises in Ashulia, Savar, on Sunday evening.
The incident occurred around 6:45 PM in the Jamgora area at the premises of Pretty Group's garment factory. The explosion happened while gas cylinders were being unloaded from the van.

A 55-year-old woman named Joynab was killed instantly when a cylinder flew 200 yards away, pierced the tin roof of a tailor shop, and struck her head. She had been visiting her daughter who works at the shop.
Five other bodies were later recovered from inside the covered van. The identities of the remaining victims have not yet been confirmed.
The blast was so powerful that it shattered the windows of the factory building and triggered a chain reaction of cylinders exploding, which spread the fire to 5-6 other nearby vehicles.
Multiple units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence arrived at the scene to bring the fire under control. Police and authorities are currently investigating the cause of the accident.

headline_marked: Fuel prices jump by [[Tk20 per litre]] across four fuel types
headline: Fuel prices jump by Tk20 per litre across four fuel types
summary: Diesel, kerosene, petrol, and octane prices increase starting Monday, as the government aims to reduce BPC's massive losses.
details: Fuel prices in Bangladesh have increased by Tk20 per litre for diesel, kerosene, petrol, and octane. The new rates, effective from Monday, September 21, set diesel at Tk135, kerosene at Tk155, petrol at Tk160, and octane at Tk165 per litre.

The Energy and Mineral Resources Division issued a notification on Sunday, September 20, confirming the price hike. Previously, these fuels were sold at Tk115 for diesel, Tk135 for kerosene, Tk140 for petrol, and Tk145 for octane.

According to the notification, international fuel prices and freight charges have risen significantly since March due to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. While global prices more than doubled, the government had not fully adjusted domestic prices in the public interest.
This delay in adjustment led to a loss of approximately Tk22,875.66 crore for the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) between March and August.

The notification further states that BPC is currently losing about Tk89 per litre on diesel alone. This results in a daily loss of approximately Tk109 crore, with potential annual losses of Tk40,000 crore for diesel.
By increasing the price by Tk20 per litre, the government expects to reduce BPC's annual losses by approximately Tk10,000 crore.
